title: Five-year Local Option Levy for Police, Fire & 911 Operations.
ballot_label: Caption: Five-year Local Option Levy for Police, Fire & 911 Operations. Question: Shall Troutdale adopt a local option levy at $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value for police, fire & 911 services? This measure may cause property taxes to increase more than three percent.
summary: Troutdale contracts for police, fire and 911 services. This five-year local option levy of $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value would fund only police, fire and 911 operations, and the Council would replace the current $25-per-month Public Safety Fee. The City says costs are rising faster than available funding and projects a $3 million gap next year growing to over $5 million by 2030.
yes_means: A yes vote approves a five-year Troutdale local option property tax levy of $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value for police, fire and 911 services.
no_means: A no vote rejects the proposed five-year levy for police, fire and 911 services.
fiscal_impact: Estimated collections: $3,556,392 (2027-28), $3,663,084 (2028-29), $3,772,977 (2029-30), $3,886,166 (2030-31), $4,002,751 (2031-32). An average home assessed at about $267,800 would pay about $428.48 a year; the levy would replace the $300-a-year ($25 per month) Public Safety Fee, for an estimated net annual increase of about $128.48.

arguments.author: City of Troutdale (explanatory statement, submitted by Sarah Skroch, City Recorder)
arguments.statement: The City's explanatory statement says current trends show a $3 million public safety funding gap next year, growing to over $5 million by 2030.
arguments.excerpt: Current trends show a $3 million funding gap next year increasing annually to over $5 million by 2030.

verification.note: Excerpt verbatim in the City explanatory statement (submitted by Sarah Skroch, City Recorder). This is neutral official text placed on the YES side.

arguments.author: Mayor David Ripma
arguments.statement: In a 2026 KATU interview, Mayor David Ripma said that if voters reject the levy the city would be in fiscal trouble and would have to figure something out.
arguments.excerpt: Ripma told KATU that if voters reject the property tax levy, the city would be in "fiscal trouble." "We'll have to figure something out," he said.

The official summary itself gives the $300 annual fee and the 'estimated net annual cost increase of approximately $128.48', so the reliance on KATU was removed and the official figures are used.
